answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic “ridge” of shared credentials—a vault address, a payment source and a synchronized timing nonce—so any new identity must inherit the full chain. When a node presents a sable‑colored proof‑of‑link, peers verify the entire ridge; missing links cause immediate isolation. An attacker therefore must duplicate every linked credential and replay the dawn‑timed nonce for each fake node, inflating cost linearly with the size of the existing network.
